notes:
Account profile: mid-market adtech company powering low-latency auction and personalization decisions. Primary ask: shave 30-50ms off current P95 while reducing per-request token cost ~20% via batching/caching/quantization guidance.

Summary of constraints and asks:
- Traffic: highly spiky, 2M reqs/day average, peak bursts 6-8x; 8k RPS sustained during ad peaks in NA.
- Latency SLO: 120ms P95 target for reranking model (90 tokens median).
- Cost sensitivity: margin-driven bidding; want predictable unit economics for each auction decision.
- Security: VPC + strict data residency controls for EU customers; SOC2 report requested.
- Model preference: open-weights Llama/Mistral family with int8/int4 quantized variants; willing to test Redwood-verified variants.
- Ops requirements: observability into token-level cost, KV cache hit rates, batching stats; auto-fallback to cheaper model when load > threshold.

Quotes from stakeholders: "If we can reduce tail without hurting quality, we'll put a reserved pool in place." — Head of ML.

Why Redwood? Team cited runtime optimizations, batching/caching tooling, and rollout features for safe canaries. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations (batch sizing, cache TTLs, quant profiles) and hosting a short focused benchmark run.

POC specifics requested: 72h mixed-workload perf run (normal day + synthetic peak bursts) using Dedicated pool, compare: baseline (current infra), Redwood hosted_dedicated non-quantized, Redwood quantized int8,int4 variants. Measure P50/P95/P99, token cost, KV cache hit rate, batching efficiency, and quality delta on a 200-sample auction set.

requirements_summary: Latency- and cost-sensitive real-time reranking for ad auctions. Needs predictable P95 <=120ms under bursty traffic, cost per decision reduction plan (20% target). Wants Redwood Optimize guidance on batch sizing, dynamic KV caching, and quantization profiles; requires bench with non-quantized and int8/int4 variants to measure quality drift.
perf_benchmark_notes: Benchmark matrix agreed: - Workloads: steady-state 2k RPS, burst 8k RPS (1min bursts), micro-batches vs continuous batching. - Metrics: P50/P95/P99, median token cost, batching efficiency (tokens per batch), cache hit rate, quality A/B on auction win-rate impact. - Success criteria: P95 <=130ms on Dedicated int8 run with <2% quality regression vs baseline.
decision_criteria: 1) Meets latency SLO under bursts 2) Cost delta per decision vs baseline <= -15% 3) Clear path to reserved capacity with SLA 4) Security artifacts (SOC2 + data residency) verified
